newsitem.title: GERMANY: IMF gold sale may be absorbed - Dresdner Bank.
newsitem.headline: IMF gold sale may be absorbed - Dresdner Bank.

text.p: International Monetary Fund gold sales might be more easily absorbed than expected, Dresdner Bank said on Friday.
"...a majority in favour of the sale...cannot be ruled out," Dresdner said in a weekly precious metals report.
It added that a compromise might be found to reconcile those in favour, including the U.S. and Britain, and those opposed, namely Germany, Italy and Switzerland.
IMF management has proposed selling around five million of the Fund's 104 million ounces of gold to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.
The IMF board was due to meet on Friday to discuss the proposal.
Dresdner said if the IMF auctioned five million ounces, or 160 tonnes, of gold over the next five years, as proposed, this would be no reason for panic.

Belgian had confirmed sales of 203 tonnes of gold last winter after selling off a huge tonnage in 1989 and 1992, the Netherlands sold 400 tonnes in 1993 and Canada was continuously selling small quantities from national reserves.
"Jewellery demand alone of 2,750 tonnes a year already exceeds mine production of 2,300," Dresdner said.
Other applications required another 875 tonnes, producing an overall deficit of 1,300 tonnes.
This needed to be covered through recycling but also through central bank sales and producers' forward sales.
"But what would happen if these sources no longer flowed?" Dresdner asked. "Perhaps we'd hear the IMF did not sell enough gold before 12 months were up."
